definitions.explanation: Drinking (usually alcohol) while standing at a counter rather than sitting, and by extension a cheap bar where customers drink this way. Such bars are common near train stations and are known for low prices and quick visits.

examples.japanese: {立|た}ち{飲|の}みの⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: We went into a stand-up bar.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{立|た}ち{飲|の}み⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{安|やす}くて→安い：00464_yasui⟧⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧がある。
examples.english: The stand-up bar in front of the station is cheap and popular.

examples.japanese: ⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧{帰|がえ}りに⟦{同僚|どうりょう}→同僚：01023_douryou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{立|た}ち{飲|の}みで⟦{一杯|いっぱい}→一杯：01793_ippai⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦{飲|の}んで→飲む：00322_nomu⟧⟦{帰|かえ}った→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧。
examples.english: On the way home from work I had just one drink with a coworker at a stand-up bar and went home.

notes:
From ⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧ (to stand) + ⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧ (to drink). Parallel to ⟦{立|た}ち{食|ぐ}い→立ち食い：08290_tachigui⟧ (eating standing up), the stand-up noodle counters found at stations. The word names both the act and the kind of bar; the bar itself is often called {立|た}ち{飲|の}み⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立|た}ち{飲|の}み⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧: stand-up bar
- {立|た}ち{飲|の}みの⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧: stand-up drinking place
- {立|た}ち{飲|の}みで⟦{一杯|いっぱい}→一杯：01793_ippai⟧: a quick drink standing up
- {角打|かくう}ち: drinking at a liquor shop's counter (a regional name for a similar custom)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Stand-up bars are associated with office workers stopping for a quick, cheap drink before the train home. Because no one sits, turnover is fast and strangers often chat across the counter.
